deterministic.title: Rotational Mechanics: Torque & Angular Momentum

task.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate torque using position vector r and force F, and relate it to angular momentum L = Iω.
required_relationships: Torque is the cross product of position and force
Angular momentum is burner product of moment of inertia and angular velocity

scene.caption: Torque τ is defined as the cross product of the position vector r and force F about a pivot O.

equations.meaning: Torque equals position vector crossed with force
Angular momentum equals moment of inertia times angular velocity
Change in angular momentum equals angular impulse

steps: Identify the pivot point O and position vector r
Determine the applied force F and its line of action
Calculate torque using τ = r × F
Relate torque to angular momentum change via time integral
points: Torque governs rotational acceleration just as force governs linear acceleration
Angular momentum L = Iω links mass distribution and rotational speed

composition.title: Rotational Mechanics
composition.framing: Relating force and position to rotational dynamics and angular momentum.

callouts.label: ΔL = ∫ τ dt
callouts.value: Change in angular momentum equals angular impulse

reasoning.explanation: Cross product defines rotational turning effect

composition.takeaway: Net torque over a time interval produces a direct change in angular momentum.
